requirements.summary: After a reset every field holds the reset value of its description.
A read-write field takes the written bits of an accepted write to its own register and keeps its value otherwise.
A read-only field never changes; a write to a register of read-only fields is answered as the bus contract of the block says.
A sticky write-one-to-clear field sets every event bit, with the event winning over a clear in the same cycle, and clears only the bits written as one.
A read returns every field at its own bit position and zero in the reserved bits.
An address outside the map answers with an error, reads as zero and changes no field.
Every generated property can be exercised: the cover goals are reached, and an environment that never starts a transfer is noticed.
The property generator is checked against tables written by hand: its correct output equals them, and each planted generator error is rejected, including those a proof alone cannot see.
